title: WHAT SERVICE COULD I SELL?
content:
A service idea usually comes from a useful thing you can do for someone else, not from finding the fanciest job title.

You may already have sellable abilities hidden inside work experience, hobbies, household responsibilities, volunteer work, technical skills, organization, communication, creative work, or problems you have learned to solve.

LOOK FOR TASKS AND RESULTS
"I worked in an office" is broad. Inside that experience might be bookkeeping, scheduling, spreadsheet cleanup, customer communication, document preparation, data entry, invoicing, or process organization.

"I am good with computers" is broad. You may actually be good at setting up devices, troubleshooting common problems, organizing files, building websites, configuring software, or teaching people how to use tools.

The useful question is: what can I DO that another person or business might reasonably want done?

YOU DO NOT NEED TO BE THE WORLD'S BEST
A service provider needs enough competence to responsibly deliver the promised service. You do not need to be the top expert in the industry. Some services do require licenses, certifications, insurance, or regulated expertise, so those requirements need independent verification before selling them.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT
If you still cannot identify a service, PDF 41 uses ChatGPT to interview you about your experience and uncover possibilities. If a service idea has already appeared, continue to PDF 42.

I NEED HELP DISCOVERING SERVICES → PDF 41.
I HAVE A SERVICE IDEA → PDF 42.

WHERE SERVICE IDEAS HIDE

People often overlook skills because the tasks feel ordinary to them. Someone who has managed a household budget for years may have strong spreadsheet and organization skills. Someone who trains new coworkers may be good at documenting processes or teaching software. Someone who maintains equipment may understand troubleshooting that others find intimidating.

Do not automatically turn every ability into a business. The purpose is to notice what you can already do, then investigate whether any of those abilities connect to a customer problem you would actually want to solve.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 41 if you need discovery help. If you already have a plausible service, move to PDF 42.
